compiled_state.description:
# The deterministic child-closure proof is computed, then hidden from the verifier

The completion precheck already computes, deterministically and exactly, whether every direct child
of a parent is closed and certified — `child_closure_findings(ticket)` returns
`(blocking, uncertified)`. For epic [rebar:e369-a449-4773-48fb] this is measured as
`blocking=0, uncertified=0`: hard proof that all 59 descendants are closed AND carry certified
signatures.

That proof is then **collapsed to a single boolean** (`certifiable`) at
`src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_ops.py:132` and routed only to the `reconcile` step. **Nothing about it
reaches the verifier's prompt** — `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/completion-verification.yaml` wires
only `context` into the `decide@then/verify` step.

## Why it matters

Epics routinely write an acceptance criterion of the form *"every child story is closed and its
change is `Verified +1` on Gerrit"* (e369's criterion #1, verbatim). The verifier is handed that
criterion with **zero evidence**, and it has no tool that can reach the answer:

* the **closure/certification half** is already proven deterministically one step earlier and is
  discarded;
* the **Gerrit half** (`Verified +1`) is not obtainable from the repository at all — no read-only
  repo tool can query Gerrit.

So the verifier must either guess, or follow its own instruction
(`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md:150-151`: *"If, after a bounded search, you cannot
find evidence that a requirement is met, record what you searched and treat it as NOT MET"*) and
FAIL a criterion that is in fact satisfied and was **already proven satisfied by deterministic code
in the same workflow run**. That is a false FAIL on a gate that SIGNS its verdict.

It also wastes budget: the verifier spends tool calls hunting for evidence that no tool can produce.

## Discovered from

[rebar:c827-2a23-cd00-473e] — while root-causing why e369's completion verification never reaches a
verdict. Recorded there and in [rebar:bf31-fd55-d28d-4b7a]'s RCA as the most likely route to a
genuine FAIL even once the run does reach a verdict.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] the deterministic child-closure/certification result (counts, and the ids of any
      unclosed/uncertified children) is surfaced to the completion verifier as evidence, inside the
      existing fenced-context delimiter so it keeps the prompt-injection boundary
- [ ] a criterion of the form "every child is closed" can be resolved from that evidence without the
      verifier making a tool call
- [ ] the Gerrit half (`Verified +1`) is explicitly addressed: either evidence is supplied, or the
      verifier is told plainly that this half is out of reach so it does not silently FAIL on it
- [ ] a test pins that the evidence appears in the verify step's inputs and that its content matches
      what `child_closure_findings` returned
- [ ] no change to the deterministic short-circuit: an UNCLOSED direct child must still block with no
      LLM call
compiled_state.title: Child-closure proof is computed deterministically then hidden from the completion verifier
